args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), checkout-api failed health checks with an 18% error rate. (v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.) Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions with a 0.2% error rate. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west and eu-west), and it's healthy again.

- **What was wrong:** the latest release, v2.3.1, was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate had also failed in staging before it went to production.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service passes health checks and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened a SEV2 for checkout-api describing the failure and the rollback, which paged the on-call engineer. It notes as follow-up that someone should find why v2.3.1 failed before it's deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
